proof_attempt_summary: Three proposal versions repaired intervention semantics, quotient labeling, and the exact-at-law output, then tried to promote the response-profile quotient with bounded audits. The quotient remained definitional and no infinite-family compression, complexity separation, or new identification capability was proved; the nonvacuous matching obstruction and shared-latent extension remain open. No D0 derivation or Lean formalization was started.
tldr: The project asks when a named equation-replacement effect in a finite uniquely solvable BGCM is identified without treating a perfect matching as automatic SCM semantics. Its proposed main result is a labelled, shared-latent response-profile realization and quotient theorem for the explicitly reconstructed postreplacement graph and its DM clusters. Constancy on the observed-law fiber and real-algebraic exact-at-\(p\)-or-countermodels are corollaries. Exhaustive binary two- and three-variable audits must demonstrate collapse of relation tables beyond latent relabeling and reuse across all block laws and the fixed graph's singleton-parent contexts; the remaining matching-completeness question is stated only on a nonempty target-preserving reducible subfamily.
gap: No located result gives a shared-latent, equation-labelled realization theorem for the pair of observational and named-intervention response maps in a finite BGCM. Matching gives causal-ordering clusters, but total functional solvability for a matched variable and preservation of the replaced equation are additional requirements. Generic polynomial search supplies an oracle, not this semantic quotient.
fill: Prove that Boolean-feasible labelled cluster response tables are exactly the quotient of admissible relation systems by equality of their two-regime solution maps, establish strict non-relabeling collapse in exhaustive bounded audits, derive identification and exact-at-law countermodel compilation as corollaries, and determine whether target-preserving matching reductions are complete on their genuinely reducible subfamily.
